## (c) The three generations come out identical

All three singular values are equal in every sector (largest spread 0.0e+00) [computed]. Reason [standard]: the three generations are the j = 1 triplet of the sphere's SO(3), acting as a rotation combined with a gauge transformation because of the flux, so SO(3) is an exact flavour symmetry. The isometry vectors (a mix of the metric and the U(1)_X field along the Killing vectors) are MASSLESS at tree level [standard, RSS 1983: Randjbar-Daemi, Salam & Strathdee], so the generation SO(3) is a gauged flavour symmetry and on the round sphere the degeneracy is exact. Squashing would break SO(3) to U(1) and give two of the three vectors a mass of order the squashing scale [standard]. Any mass hierarchy between generations therefore needs an input that breaks SO(3), such as a squashed sphere, a rugby ball with conical tips, or a localised source [assumed]. None is added here.

## (d) U(1)_X needs Green-Schwarz

4D U(1)_X anomalies over three generations, with nu^c, T = 1 normalisation [computed, same as RESULTS_alt.md criterion 4]: SU(3)^2 X = 0, SU(2)^2 X = 12, Y^2 X = -6, Y X^2 = 0, X^3 = 0, grav^2 X = 0.
Irreducible 6D tr R^4: 8 Weyl fields at Gamma_7 = -1 against 8 at +1 [computed, same as RESULTS_alt.md criterion 5].
SU(2)^2 X and Y^2 X do not cancel. They are cancelled by a Green-Schwarz term, which makes U(1)_X a massive Z' [standard, not computed]. Its mass depends on the Green-Schwarz coupling, so the Z' scale is [assumed].
Gauged SO(3) check (Helios's bonus check, weighting corrected by Venus) [computed; Venus confirmed]: every fermion zero mode sits in the same j = 1 triplet of SU(2)_KK, whose index is T(3) = 2 (doublet normalised to 1/2). Summing over the 4D left-handed fields, each counted once: A[SU(2)_KK^2 Y] = T(3) * Sum Y = 2 x 0 = 0. A[SU(2)_KK^2 X] = T(3) * Sum X = 2 * (8 * (+1) + 8 * (-1)) = 0, with the +1 group Q (6), L (2) and the -1 group u^c (3), d^c (3), e^c (1), nu^c (1); without nu^c it would be 2 * 1 = 2, so this one needs nu^c. Anomalies with exactly one SU(2)_KK vertex vanish because the generators are traceless; SU(2) has no cubic anomaly; the Witten anomaly does not apply because the isospin is integer. So gauging the generation SO(3) adds no new anomaly.
